frozenCase.displayName: Operative contamination and a later wound infection
frozenCase.presentation: Wesley Donovan, a 60-year-old man, returns to the clinic after a superficial wound infection following bowel resection. During the operation, bowel contents spilled when the planned enterotomy was extended; the operative photographs show contamination of the field before closure. The infection team is comparing the new prevention program with an earlier period using wound-class strata. His record exposes a change in how the data were coded.

sourceLabels: Protocol for the Surveillance of Surgical Site Infection: wound class
Analyzing and Interpreting Data

decisionNodes.stem: Which data-preparation plan is needed before the team compares infection rates in Wesley Donovan's operative wound-class stratum?

answerChoices.label: Reconstruct both periods from intraoperative findings
answerChoices.rationale: Later infection selectively changes the new-period predictor; reconstructing the same operation-time variable restores comparable classification without relabeling the outcome.

answerChoices.label: Retain final classes and adjust for the number of readmissions
answerChoices.rationale: A count adjustment does not undo selective movement of infections between operative strata.

answerChoices.label: Reconstruct both periods from later readmission reports
answerChoices.rationale: Applying outcome-driven recoding to both periods makes the coding rule consistent but still moves infected cases out of their original risk strata.

decisionNodes.explanation: Classify contamination at the operation and preserve the later infection as an outcome. Gross operative spillage is not converted retrospectively into a pre-existing dirty/infected operation because a wound later becomes infected. In the new-period dataset, selectively moving infected cases changes the denominator and outcomes within the apparent original class. Reconstruct comparable operation-time classifications before comparing rates; this does not by itself prove the prevention program caused any benefit. The audit-bias application is an explicit local synthesis, not a published performance estimate.

decisionNodes.stem: What is needed before additional research-only tissue sampling when Lily Clay has consented only to a clinical endoscopic examination for Barrett esophagus?

answerChoices.label: Use a signed research form as the entire consent process
answerChoices.rationale: A signed research form alone is not the entire consent process. The participant needs the relevant understandable discussion and voluntary choice for the added activity.

answerChoices.label: Extend the clinical consent to cover the extra sampling
answerChoices.rationale: Clinical consent does not expand automatically to an additional undisclosed research procedure. Extending its label does not supply the missing research discussion or applicable oversight.

answerChoices.label: Ask the treating surgeon to authorize the extra sampling
answerChoices.rationale: The surgeon's approval is not the patient's research permission. It does not replace the appropriate consent process and applicable oversight.

answerChoices.label: Complete an appropriate research consent process
answerChoices.rationale: The additional procedure is research-only and was not discussed in the treatment consent. Address its purpose, added procedure, and voluntary choice through appropriate research consent and oversight.

decisionNodes.explanation: Complete the appropriate research consent process and applicable oversight before the additional sampling. The clinical-treatment signature does not automatically cover this undisclosed research-only procedure.
decisionNodes.teachingPoint: Consent to treatment does not automatically authorize an additional research-only procedure. The research purpose, added procedure, and voluntary choice need appropriate research consent and applicable oversight. A signature has a scope: adding a research activity requires addressing that activity, rather than extending the clinical form by assumption or treating another form as the conversation.

decisionNodes.stem: What should the team prioritize after Olivia Sterling develops symptoms from an unintended medication while preparing for breast-cyst aspiration, before clinical help is arranged?

answerChoices.label: Arrange immediate assessment and patient care
answerChoices.rationale: The patient is symptomatic after an unintended medication. Immediate assessment and appropriate care take priority, with disclosure and reporting accompanying the response.

answerChoices.label: Verify the medication record before calling for clinical help
answerChoices.rationale: The team already recognizes an unintended medication and new symptoms. Record checking must not become a reason to delay calling for the clinical help required.

answerChoices.label: Contact the disclosure lead before arranging assessment
answerChoices.rationale: Disclosure coordination does not need to come before arranging clinical help. The symptomatic patient requires assessment and care now.

answerChoices.label: Complete the safety report to obtain a review referral
answerChoices.rationale: Completing an incident report first delays needed assessment. The form documents the event; it is not the clinical response to the symptoms.

decisionNodes.explanation: Arrange immediate assessment and patient care. Disclosure and safety reporting remain part of the response, but completing those steps first must not delay help for the symptomatic patient.
decisionNodes.teachingPoint: Immediate patient safety and appropriate treatment take priority when symptoms develop after an unintended medication. Arrange assessment and care while candid disclosure and reporting accompany the response. Remember that an incident form records the event; it does not treat the patient. Administrative or disclosure coordination should not delay the indicated clinical help.

decisionNodes.stem: Which diagnostic plan should the hospital use next for Wesley Underwood's vomiting?

answerChoices.label: Contrast fluoroscopy with pyloric transit mapping
answerChoices.rationale: Fluoroscopy can characterize transit, but contrast already passes and it would not characterize the irregular mural lesion histologically.

answerChoices.label: Repeat endoscopy with pyloric biopsy
answerChoices.rationale: The first procedure ended because of retained contents, not an impassable proven stricture. Decompression changes the acquisition conditions, and the irregular structural lesion warrants direct assessment and tissue.

answerChoices.label: Prepared four-hour gastric-emptying scintigraphy
answerChoices.rationale: This is the appropriate physiology protocol after structural exclusion; diabetes and retained food do not supply that prerequisite.

decisionNodes.explanation: Retained food in diabetes does not establish gastroparesis. The first examination was preparation-limited; decompression and persistent contrast passage support a prepared repeat examination rather than treating prior termination as proof that endoscopic access is impossible. Assess and sample the irregular pyloric lesion before moving to emptying physiology. This is a diagnostic plan, not an instruction to force a scope through a tight obstruction.

decisionNodes.stem: What is the most likely diagnosis after this integrated cutaneous small-cell tumor workup?
decisionNodes.explanation: The correct answer is “Merkel cell carcinoma.” A primary cutaneous neuroendocrine carcinoma with this integrated assessment fits Merkel cell carcinoma. The specialist workup does not support a pulmonary primary. The provided integrated phenotype is not melanocytic. The phenotype is epithelial and neuroendocrine rather than lymphoid.

answerChoices.label: Defer regional staging until after wider excision

decisionNodes.explanation: The correct answer is “Coordinate specialist sentinel-node staging.” Early coordination can preserve mapping while assessing occult regional disease. Clinical node negativity is not pathologic node negativity. Coordinating sentinel mapping before wider excision can preserve staging options. A clinically negative candidate is considered for sentinel staging rather than automatic complete dissection.

decisionNodes.stem: Which data-preparation plan is needed before the team compares infection rates in Wesley Donovan's operative wound-class stratum?

answerChoices.label: Reconstruct both periods from intraoperative findings
answerChoices.rationale: Later infection selectively changes the new-period predictor; reconstructing the same operation-time variable restores comparable classification without relabeling the outcome.

answerChoices.label: Retain final classes and adjust for the number of readmissions
answerChoices.rationale: A count adjustment does not undo selective movement of infections between operative strata.

answerChoices.label: Reconstruct both periods from later readmission reports
answerChoices.rationale: Applying outcome-driven recoding to both periods makes the coding rule consistent but still moves infected cases out of their original risk strata.

decisionNodes.explanation: Classify contamination at the operation and preserve the later infection as an outcome. Gross operative spillage is not converted retrospectively into a pre-existing dirty/infected operation because a wound later becomes infected. In the new-period dataset, selectively moving infected cases changes the denominator and outcomes within the apparent original class. Reconstruct comparable operation-time classifications before comparing rates; this does not by itself prove the prevention program caused any benefit. The audit-bias application is an explicit local synthesis, not a published performance estimate.

decisionNodes.stem: What is needed before additional research-only tissue sampling when Lily Clay has consented only to a clinical endoscopic examination for Barrett esophagus?

answerChoices.label: Use a signed research form as the entire consent process
answerChoices.rationale: A signed research form alone is not the entire consent process. The participant needs the relevant understandable discussion and voluntary choice for the added activity.

answerChoices.label: Extend the clinical consent to cover the extra sampling
answerChoices.rationale: Clinical consent does not expand automatically to an additional undisclosed research procedure. Extending its label does not supply the missing research discussion or applicable oversight.

answerChoices.label: Ask the treating surgeon to authorize the extra sampling
answerChoices.rationale: The surgeon's approval is not the patient's research permission. It does not replace the appropriate consent process and applicable oversight.

answerChoices.label: Complete an appropriate research consent process
answerChoices.rationale: The additional procedure is research-only and was not discussed in the treatment consent. Address its purpose, added procedure, and voluntary choice through appropriate research consent and oversight.

decisionNodes.explanation: Complete the appropriate research consent process and applicable oversight before the additional sampling. The clinical-treatment signature does not automatically cover this undisclosed research-only procedure.
decisionNodes.teachingPoint: Consent to treatment does not automatically authorize an additional research-only procedure. The research purpose, added procedure, and voluntary choice need appropriate research consent and applicable oversight. A signature has a scope: adding a research activity requires addressing that activity, rather than extending the clinical form by assumption or treating another form as the conversation.

decisionNodes.stem: What should the team prioritize after Olivia Sterling develops symptoms from an unintended medication while preparing for breast-cyst aspiration, before clinical help is arranged?

answerChoices.label: Arrange immediate assessment and patient care
answerChoices.rationale: The patient is symptomatic after an unintended medication. Immediate assessment and appropriate care take priority, with disclosure and reporting accompanying the response.

answerChoices.label: Verify the medication record before calling for clinical help
answerChoices.rationale: The team already recognizes an unintended medication and new symptoms. Record checking must not become a reason to delay calling for the clinical help required.

answerChoices.label: Contact the disclosure lead before arranging assessment
answerChoices.rationale: Disclosure coordination does not need to come before arranging clinical help. The symptomatic patient requires assessment and care now.

answerChoices.label: Complete the safety report to obtain a review referral
answerChoices.rationale: Completing an incident report first delays needed assessment. The form documents the event; it is not the clinical response to the symptoms.

decisionNodes.explanation: Arrange immediate assessment and patient care. Disclosure and safety reporting remain part of the response, but completing those steps first must not delay help for the symptomatic patient.
decisionNodes.teachingPoint: Immediate patient safety and appropriate treatment take priority when symptoms develop after an unintended medication. Arrange assessment and care while candid disclosure and reporting accompany the response. Remember that an incident form records the event; it does not treat the patient. Administrative or disclosure coordination should not delay the indicated clinical help.

decisionNodes.stem: Which diagnostic plan should the hospital use next for Wesley Underwood's vomiting?

answerChoices.label: Contrast fluoroscopy with pyloric transit mapping
answerChoices.rationale: Fluoroscopy can characterize transit, but contrast already passes and it would not characterize the irregular mural lesion histologically.

answerChoices.label: Repeat endoscopy with pyloric biopsy
answerChoices.rationale: The first procedure ended because of retained contents, not an impassable proven stricture. Decompression changes the acquisition conditions, and the irregular structural lesion warrants direct assessment and tissue.

answerChoices.label: Prepared four-hour gastric-emptying scintigraphy
answerChoices.rationale: This is the appropriate physiology protocol after structural exclusion; diabetes and retained food do not supply that prerequisite.

decisionNodes.explanation: Retained food in diabetes does not establish gastroparesis. The first examination was preparation-limited; decompression and persistent contrast passage support a prepared repeat examination rather than treating prior termination as proof that endoscopic access is impossible. Assess and sample the irregular pyloric lesion before moving to emptying physiology. This is a diagnostic plan, not an instruction to force a scope through a tight obstruction.

decisionNodes.explanation: The correct answer is “Coordinate specialist sentinel-node staging.” Early coordination can preserve mapping while assessing occult regional disease. decisionNodes.stem: Which set lists a process measure, the intended clinical outcome measure and a balancing measure, in that order, for the lung-cancer screening program pilot?

answerChoices.label: Completed program screening; extra diagnostic visits; missed cancers at follow-up
answerChoices.rationale: Extra diagnostic visits check burden, while missed cancers measure the aim. This ordering swaps the outcome and balancing positions.

answerChoices.label: Completed program screening; missed cancers at follow-up; extra diagnostic visits
answerChoices.rationale: Completed screening tracks delivery, missed cancers track the program’s diagnostic aim, and extra diagnostic visits check the additional assessment burden.

answerChoices.label: Screening invitations sent; screening visits completed; extra diagnostic visits
answerChoices.rationale: Invitations and completed screening visits both track program activity. This set does not measure missed cancers, the stated clinical aim.

answerChoices.label: Missed cancers at follow-up; completed program screening; extra diagnostic visits
answerChoices.rationale: Missed cancers are the outcome and completed screening is process. This set places those two measures in the reverse order requested.

decisionNodes.explanation: Use completed program screening as process, missed cancers at follow-up as outcome, and extra diagnostic visits as balance. Attendance counts do not substitute for the diagnostic aim.
decisionNodes.teachingPoint: Screening activity and screening success need different measures. Completed screens track delivery; missed cancers at follow-up track the stated diagnostic aim; extra diagnostic visits check burden. Remember to count both what the program does and what it misses. Invitation or attendance totals alone do not establish that the clinical aim improved.

frozenCase.displayName: Act and iterate after a PDSA test and Choose process, outcome, and balancing measures
frozenCase.presentation: Marley, the lung-screening improvement lead, reviews a new lung-cancer screening program for eligible adults. The pilot aims to reduce missed lung cancers at protocol follow-up and may require extra diagnostic visits. Colleagues propose different combinations of measures for the report. The team is planning what to record before testing the unnamed program; no benefit or screening-test performance is supplied.
sourceLabels: Plan-Do-Check-Act Cycle
Chapter 6. Track Performance with Metrics
Screening for Lung Cancer

decisionNodes.stem: Which set lists a process measure, the intended clinical outcome measure and a balancing measure, in that order, for the lung-cancer screening program pilot?

answerChoices.label: Completed program screening; extra diagnostic visits; missed cancers at follow-up
answerChoices.rationale: Extra diagnostic visits check burden, while missed cancers measure the aim. This ordering swaps the outcome and balancing positions.

answerChoices.label: Completed program screening; missed cancers at follow-up; extra diagnostic visits
answerChoices.rationale: Completed screening tracks delivery, missed cancers track the program’s diagnostic aim, and extra diagnostic visits check the additional assessment burden.

answerChoices.label: Screening invitations sent; screening visits completed; extra diagnostic visits
answerChoices.rationale: Invitations and completed screening visits both track program activity. This set does not measure missed cancers, the stated clinical aim.

answerChoices.label: Missed cancers at follow-up; completed program screening; extra diagnostic visits
answerChoices.rationale: Missed cancers are the outcome and completed screening is process. This set places those two measures in the reverse order requested.

decisionNodes.explanation: Use completed program screening as process, missed cancers at follow-up as outcome, and extra diagnostic visits as balance. Attendance counts do not substitute for the diagnostic aim.
decisionNodes.teachingPoint: Screening activity and screening success need different measures. Completed screens track delivery; missed cancers at follow-up track the stated diagnostic aim; extra diagnostic visits check burden. Remember to count both what the program does and what it misses. Invitation or attendance totals alone do not establish that the clinical aim improved.

exhibit.title: Investigational clinical pilot — illustrative measurement plan
exhibit.body: An authorized pilot of an unnamed investigational lung-cancer screening program for lung-cancer screening aims to improve missed cancers at protocol follow-up. The team is concerned about extra diagnostic visits. This protocol is invented for practice and supplies no real efficacy, diagnostic accuracy or patient-specific prediction.

decisionNodes.stem: What should guide the authorized surrogate's operative decision for Gavin Young's acute cholecystitis when known patient wishes differ from the surrogate's own preference?

answerChoices.label: Use the patient's known preferences
answerChoices.rationale: Specific prior discussions identify what this patient would choose in these circumstances. Substituted judgment uses those known wishes rather than the surrogate's own preference.

answerChoices.label: Use the surrogate's preferred treatment plan
answerChoices.rationale: The surrogate represents the patient's known perspective. Personally favoring treatment does not justify replacing the patient's specific contrary wishes.

answerChoices.label: Use the family's agreed treatment preference
answerChoices.rationale: Family agreement does not displace a known patient preference. Counting relatives' choices answers whose plan is popular, rather than what this patient would choose.

answerChoices.label: Use the option with the greatest expected benefit
answerChoices.rationale: Best-interest deliberation is the fallback when wishes cannot be determined. Here known preferences supply the patient's perspective rather than leaving it unknown.

decisionNodes.explanation: Use the patient's known preferences through substituted judgment. The surrogate's own preference does not replace specific prior wishes about these circumstances.
decisionNodes.teachingPoint: Substituted judgment asks what this patient would choose, using known preferences and values. It does not ask what the surrogate would choose for themselves or what most relatives prefer. Here specific prior wishes are available. Remember that the surrogate represents the patient's perspective; best-interest deliberation is the fallback when that perspective cannot be determined.

frozenCase.presentation: Marley, the lung-screening improvement lead, reviews a new lung-cancer screening program for eligible adults. The pilot aims to reduce missed lung cancers at protocol follow-up and may require extra diagnostic visits. Colleagues propose different combinations of measures for the report. The team is planning what to record before testing the unnamed program; no benefit or screening-test performance is supplied.
sourceLabels: Plan-Do-Check-Act Cycle
Chapter 6. Track Performance with Metrics
Screening for Lung Cancer

decisionNodes.stem: Which set lists a process measure, the intended clinical outcome measure and a balancing measure, in that order, for the lung-cancer screening program pilot?

answerChoices.label: Completed program screening; extra diagnostic visits; missed cancers at follow-up
answerChoices.rationale: Extra diagnostic visits check burden, while missed cancers measure the aim. This ordering swaps the outcome and balancing positions.

answerChoices.label: Completed program screening; missed cancers at follow-up; extra diagnostic visits
answerChoices.rationale: Completed screening tracks delivery, missed cancers track the program’s diagnostic aim, and extra diagnostic visits check the additional assessment burden.

answerChoices.label: Screening invitations sent; screening visits completed; extra diagnostic visits
answerChoices.rationale: Invitations and completed screening visits both track program activity. This set does not measure missed cancers, the stated clinical aim.

answerChoices.label: Missed cancers at follow-up; completed program screening; extra diagnostic visits
answerChoices.rationale: Missed cancers are the outcome and completed screening is process. This set places those two measures in the reverse order requested.

decisionNodes.explanation: Use completed program screening as process, missed cancers at follow-up as outcome, and extra diagnostic visits as balance. Attendance counts do not substitute for the diagnostic aim.
decisionNodes.teachingPoint: Screening activity and screening success need different measures. Completed screens track delivery; missed cancers at follow-up track the stated diagnostic aim; extra diagnostic visits check burden. Remember to count both what the program does and what it misses. Invitation or attendance totals alone do not establish that the clinical aim improved.

decisionNodes.explanation: The correct answer is “Use subtotal cholecystectomy as a bailout.” Subtotal surgery can avoid dangerous dissection of unidentified structures. Presumed identity is insufficient when the critical view cannot be obtained. Unsafe anatomic identification calls for a bailout rather than hazardous further dissection. Seeing two structures does not establish the critical view.

decisionNodes.stem: Which discussion focus fits healthcare FMEA of the planned allergy-record workflow that Kiara Everett asks about?

answerChoices.label: Contributors to a completed allergy-recording event
answerChoices.rationale: That focus starts with a past event and fits the retrospective purpose of RCA. The described meeting is about a planned workflow.

answerChoices.label: Potential failures before a problem occurs
answerChoices.rationale: Healthcare FMEA examines how the planned process could fail before those problems occur. It does not require a completed event as its starting point.

answerChoices.label: Prior patients' satisfaction with the allergy-recording encounter
answerChoices.rationale: Satisfaction may be another question, but it does not describe healthcare FMEA's stated task of anticipating potential process failures.

answerChoices.label: Individual blame for a completed allergy-recording error
answerChoices.rationale: Blame for a past error neither describes the prospective process task nor supplies its focus on potential failures.

decisionNodes.explanation: Focus on potential failures before the allergy-recording workflow starts. That prospective process purpose defines the healthcare FMEA task described here, without requiring a previous allergy-recording error.
decisionNodes.teachingPoint: Healthcare FMEA asks how a planned process might fail before those problems occur. This meeting therefore focuses on potential allergy-recording failures, rather than reconstructing a past event. Remember: look ahead at the process. That is a method classification, not a promise of zero risk or a complete set of scoring and safeguard instructions.

frozenCase.displayName: Act and iterate after a PDSA test and Choose process, outcome, and balancing measures
frozenCase.presentation: Marley, the lung-screening improvement lead, reviews a new lung-cancer screening program for eligible adults. The pilot aims to reduce missed lung cancers at protocol follow-up and may require extra diagnostic visits. Colleagues propose different combinations of measures for the report. The team is planning what to record before testing the unnamed program; no benefit or screening-test performance is supplied.
sourceLabels: Plan-Do-Check-Act Cycle
Chapter 6. Track Performance with Metrics
Screening for Lung Cancer

decisionNodes.stem: Which set lists a process measure, the intended clinical outcome measure and a balancing measure, in that order, for the lung-cancer screening program pilot?

answerChoices.label: Completed program screening; extra diagnostic visits; missed cancers at follow-up
answerChoices.rationale: Extra diagnostic visits check burden, while missed cancers measure the aim. This ordering swaps the outcome and balancing positions.

answerChoices.label: Completed program screening; missed cancers at follow-up; extra diagnostic visits
answerChoices.rationale: Completed screening tracks delivery, missed cancers track the program’s diagnostic aim, and extra diagnostic visits check the additional assessment burden.

answerChoices.label: Screening invitations sent; screening visits completed; extra diagnostic visits
answerChoices.rationale: Invitations and completed screening visits both track program activity. This set does not measure missed cancers, the stated clinical aim.

answerChoices.label: Missed cancers at follow-up; completed program screening; extra diagnostic visits
answerChoices.rationale: Missed cancers are the outcome and completed screening is process. This set places those two measures in the reverse order requested.

decisionNodes.explanation: Use completed program screening as process, missed cancers at follow-up as outcome, and extra diagnostic visits as balance. Attendance counts do not substitute for the diagnostic aim.
decisionNodes.teachingPoint: Screening activity and screening success need different measures. Completed screens track delivery; missed cancers at follow-up track the stated diagnostic aim; extra diagnostic visits check burden. Remember to count both what the program does and what it misses. Invitation or attendance totals alone do not establish that the clinical aim improved.

decisionNodes.stem: Which operative completion plan should be used for Maya Barlow?

answerChoices.label: Fenestrating subtotal cholecystectomy
answerChoices.rationale: The anatomy calls for a bailout rather than continued total dissection, and the remaining wall is not a sound basis for a closed remnant. An open-remnant subtotal strategy with appropriate drainage is the offered fit.

answerChoices.label: Reconstituting subtotal cholecystectomy
answerChoices.rationale: This is a genuine subtotal alternative, but it requires a safely closable remnant; the actual wall quality changes that choice.

answerChoices.label: Fundus-first total cholecystectomy
answerChoices.rationale: A top-down total operation does not itself resolve the fused lower anatomy or justify continuing to the uncertain hilum.

answerChoices.label: Divide the two visible biliary structures
Clip and divide the presumed cystic duct

decisionNodes.explanation: The correct answer is “Use subtotal cholecystectomy as a bailout.” Subtotal surgery can avoid dangerous dissection of unidentified structures. Presumed identity is insufficient when the critical view cannot be obtained. Unsafe anatomic identification calls for a bailout rather than hazardous further dissection. Seeing two structures does not establish the critical view.

frozenCase.displayName: Act and iterate after a PDSA test and Choose process, outcome, and balancing measures
frozenCase.presentation: Marley, the lung-screening improvement lead, reviews a new lung-cancer screening program for eligible adults. The pilot aims to reduce missed lung cancers at protocol follow-up and may require extra diagnostic visits. Colleagues propose different combinations of measures for the report. The team is planning what to record before testing the unnamed program; no benefit or screening-test performance is supplied.
sourceLabels: Plan-Do-Check-Act Cycle
Chapter 6. Track Performance with Metrics
Screening for Lung Cancer

decisionNodes.stem: Which set lists a process measure, the intended clinical outcome measure and a balancing measure, in that order, for the lung-cancer screening program pilot?

answerChoices.label: Completed program screening; extra diagnostic visits; missed cancers at follow-up
answerChoices.rationale: Extra diagnostic visits check burden, while missed cancers measure the aim. This ordering swaps the outcome and balancing positions.

answerChoices.label: Completed program screening; missed cancers at follow-up; extra diagnostic visits
answerChoices.rationale: Completed screening tracks delivery, missed cancers track the program’s diagnostic aim, and extra diagnostic visits check the additional assessment burden.

answerChoices.label: Screening invitations sent; screening visits completed; extra diagnostic visits
answerChoices.rationale: Invitations and completed screening visits both track program activity. This set does not measure missed cancers, the stated clinical aim.

answerChoices.label: Missed cancers at follow-up; completed program screening; extra diagnostic visits
answerChoices.rationale: Missed cancers are the outcome and completed screening is process. This set places those two measures in the reverse order requested.

decisionNodes.explanation: Use completed program screening as process, missed cancers at follow-up as outcome, and extra diagnostic visits as balance. Attendance counts do not substitute for the diagnostic aim.
decisionNodes.teachingPoint: Screening activity and screening success need different measures. Completed screens track delivery; missed cancers at follow-up track the stated diagnostic aim; extra diagnostic visits check burden. Remember to count both what the program does and what it misses. Invitation or attendance totals alone do not establish that the clinical aim improved.

frozenCase.presentation: Marley, the lung-screening improvement lead, reviews a new lung-cancer screening program for eligible adults. The pilot aims to reduce missed lung cancers at protocol follow-up and may require extra diagnostic visits. Colleagues propose different combinations of measures for the report. The team is planning what to record before testing the unnamed program; no benefit or screening-test performance is supplied.
sourceLabels: Plan-Do-Check-Act Cycle
Chapter 6. Track Performance with Metrics
Screening for Lung Cancer

decisionNodes.stem: Which set lists a process measure, the intended clinical outcome measure and a balancing measure, in that order, for the lung-cancer screening program pilot?

answerChoices.label: Completed program screening; extra diagnostic visits; missed cancers at follow-up
answerChoices.rationale: Extra diagnostic visits check burden, while missed cancers measure the aim. This ordering swaps the outcome and balancing positions.

answerChoices.label: Completed program screening; missed cancers at follow-up; extra diagnostic visits
answerChoices.rationale: Completed screening tracks delivery, missed cancers track the program’s diagnostic aim, and extra diagnostic visits check the additional assessment burden.

answerChoices.label: Screening invitations sent; screening visits completed; extra diagnostic visits
answerChoices.rationale: Invitations and completed screening visits both track program activity. This set does not measure missed cancers, the stated clinical aim.

answerChoices.label: Missed cancers at follow-up; completed program screening; extra diagnostic visits
answerChoices.rationale: Missed cancers are the outcome and completed screening is process. This set places those two measures in the reverse order requested.

decisionNodes.explanation: Use completed program screening as process, missed cancers at follow-up as outcome, and extra diagnostic visits as balance. Attendance counts do not substitute for the diagnostic aim.
decisionNodes.teachingPoint: Screening activity and screening success need different measures. Completed screens track delivery; missed cancers at follow-up track the stated diagnostic aim; extra diagnostic visits check burden. Remember to count both what the program does and what it misses. Invitation or attendance totals alone do not establish that the clinical aim improved.

frozenCase.presentation: Marley, the lung-screening improvement lead, reviews a new lung-cancer screening program for eligible adults. The pilot aims to reduce missed lung cancers at protocol follow-up and may require extra diagnostic visits. Colleagues propose different combinations of measures for the report. The team is planning what to record before testing the unnamed program; no benefit or screening-test performance is supplied.
sourceLabels: Plan-Do-Check-Act Cycle
Chapter 6. Track Performance with Metrics
Screening for Lung Cancer

decisionNodes.stem: Which set lists a process measure, the intended clinical outcome measure and a balancing measure, in that order, for the lung-cancer screening program pilot?

answerChoices.label: Completed program screening; extra diagnostic visits; missed cancers at follow-up
answerChoices.rationale: Extra diagnostic visits check burden, while missed cancers measure the aim. This ordering swaps the outcome and balancing positions.

answerChoices.label: Completed program screening; missed cancers at follow-up; extra diagnostic visits
answerChoices.rationale: Completed screening tracks delivery, missed cancers track the program’s diagnostic aim, and extra diagnostic visits check the additional assessment burden.

answerChoices.label: Screening invitations sent; screening visits completed; extra diagnostic visits
answerChoices.rationale: Invitations and completed screening visits both track program activity. This set does not measure missed cancers, the stated clinical aim.

answerChoices.label: Missed cancers at follow-up; completed program screening; extra diagnostic visits
answerChoices.rationale: Missed cancers are the outcome and completed screening is process. This set places those two measures in the reverse order requested.

decisionNodes.explanation: Use completed program screening as process, missed cancers at follow-up as outcome, and extra diagnostic visits as balance. Attendance counts do not substitute for the diagnostic aim.
decisionNodes.teachingPoint: Screening activity and screening success need different measures. Completed screens track delivery; missed cancers at follow-up track the stated diagnostic aim; extra diagnostic visits check burden. Remember to count both what the program does and what it misses. Invitation or attendance totals alone do not establish that the clinical aim improved.

Start lifelong cinacalcet routinely for every confirmed case
Perform focused parathyroidectomy for the inherited disorder

decisionNodes.explanation: Confirmed uncomplicated FHH is generally benign and is managed with reassurance and observation. Routine parathyroid surgery is avoided because it usually does not correct the inherited disorder.

decisionNodes.stem: Which report of the pressure study should accompany Zane Whitaker’s timed esophagram request?

answerChoices.label: Absent esophageal body contractility with impaired junction relaxation
answerChoices.rationale: This mistakes the quiet clustered-swallow phase for baseline failure and the presence of dysphagia for junction obstruction. Traveling baseline waves and the recorded relaxation behavior contradict those claims.

answerChoices.label: Reduced post-swallow reserve with preserved junction relaxation
answerChoices.rationale: The software-integrated recovery responses do not augment the baseline despite taller peaks. Baseline propagation and the liquid-load relaxation observations do not establish absent body contractility or impaired junction relaxation.

answerChoices.label: Preserved post-swallow reserve with preserved junction relaxation
answerChoices.rationale: The junction component fits, but peak height is not the integrated contractile response. The measured recovery integrals do not demonstrate augmentation.

decisionNodes.explanation: Read the separate measurements for their separate purposes. The integrated post-sequence contraction, rather than its peak alone, is the reserve comparison. The baseline waves show propagation, and the junction trace during liquid loading does not support impaired relaxation. Report reduced reserve with preserved relaxation. The common timed-esophagram request assesses actual emptying; this question does not claim that a reserve result selects barium over every other investigation or proves the cause of dysphagia.

decisionNodes.stem: Which communication approach should be used for Ruby Anderson's nonurgent neck-node observation plan when her father agrees but she wants the plan explained?

answerChoices.label: Explain to Ruby and invite her questions
answerChoices.rationale: Ruby explicitly says she does not understand. Address her directly with an appropriate explanation and invitation for questions and assent, while retaining her father's involvement.

answerChoices.label: Accept Ruby's silence and begin the clinic plan
answerChoices.rationale: Eventual silence does not establish understanding. The response should give Ruby a meaningful opportunity to understand the plan and express questions or views.

answerChoices.label: Confirm with Thomas and begin the clinic plan
answerChoices.rationale: Thomas's agreement does not resolve Ruby's stated lack of understanding. Confirming only his view leaves the child's own participation unanswered.

answerChoices.label: Postpone Ruby's involvement until she is older
answerChoices.rationale: Participation should match Ruby's understanding now. Deferring all involvement to a fixed older age bypasses the understandable discussion she is requesting.

decisionNodes.explanation: Include Ruby directly, explain the plan understandably, and invite questions and developmentally appropriate assent with her father involved. Her ethical participation and legal consent authority remain separate considerations.
decisionNodes.teachingPoint: A child's voice can be missed even when a parent is engaged and supportive. Explain the plan directly to Ruby, check understanding, and invite her questions and developmentally appropriate assent with Thomas involved. Remember that parental agreement and child participation address different needs. This ethical participation does not settle jurisdiction-specific legal consent authority.

an antithyroid drug. She is stable and asks about RAI if the outside records
confirm that overt hyperthyroidism returned after a documented remission. The
clinician is reviewing her follow-up course after withdrawal before counseling
her about treatment options.

decisionNodes.stem:
Which follow-up course in this patient's records best supports
discussing RAI as a definitive option?

answerChoices.label: Thyroid function remained normal after medication withdrawal
Symptoms returned while thyroid function remained normal
Overt hyperthyroidism returned after a documented remission
Thyroid hormone levels remained low after medication withdrawal

decisionNodes.explanation:
Confirmed recurrence of overt Graves hyperthyroidism after
antithyroid-drug withdrawal is a setting in which RAI may be considered as a
definitive option. Normal thyroid function, symptoms without biochemical
recurrence, or persistently low thyroid hormone levels do not establish that
recurrent hyperthyroid setting.

categories.formula: Mean per-minute effective morale of all employed staff; empty workforce = 0
categories.improvementHint: Pay wages, use praise/coffee, complete breaks and management rounds, and retain honest ownership support.

categories.formula: Sum of final scored-patient satisfaction / all scored completions and walkouts in the window
categories.improvementHint: Answer correctly, attend patients promptly and keep facilities clean and accessible. Use actual garden/Executive comfort; walkouts stay in the sample.

categories.formula: 100 × [0.5 × (1 − overdue queue-minutes / queue-minutes) + 0.5 × completed / (completed + walkouts)]
categories.improvementHint: Staff check-in, maintain paths/seats/care capacity and answer ready questions. Prescribed processing, travel and external-result clocks are excluded.

categories.formula: 100 × [0.5 × fully paid positive bills / positive bills + 0.5 × clip(operating net / (0.05 × operating gross))]
categories.improvementHint: Pay every bill and build real profitable services within demand. Stock is deducted once; capital spending, reserves, grants and room sales cannot improve operating profit.

categories.formula: 100 × correct first submissions / (all first submissions + presented but unanswered questions)
categories.improvementHint: Review existing explanations and answer every presented game question correctly. Wrong first answers and unanswered questions remain; this compares stored game keys, not real clinical competence.
